messages:
anya: FYI saw a weird regression when bringing up a new spm->bpe converted model. evals pass on HF artifacts but our runtime shows kv-cache misalignments and some logits drift during quant runs.
ben_reid: can you paste the minimal repro/logs?
anya: log excerpt: `ERROR runtime: kv_cache_index mismatch expected=456 got=457 at layer=8`
anya: tokenizer ids around the region: `[500, 501, 502, 504, 505]` — notice 503 is missing after conversion.
lisa_ml: hmm missing id in vocab usually means merges/vocab ordering changed during conversion. spm suffix pieces sometimes get turned into new tokens that are appended not inserted, shifting expected offsets. :thinking_face:
kevin: did you run the conversion with any special token remap flags? we recently added `--reserve-specials` to keep reserved ids contiguous.
anya: I used our standard script `hf2redwood --model-dir /tmp/mymodel --out /tmp/mymodel-redwood` (no extra flags).
ben_reid: quick check: open `tokenizer.json` and `vocab.txt` from the converted artifact. are system/reserved tokens in the first N slots? if not, that's the source.
anya: attaching snippets:```
# token id -> token
500: "t",
501: "ing",
502: "▁end",
504: "er",
505: "s"
```
lisa_ml: that `▁end` suffixpiece is a sentencepiece leftover. when we collapse to BPE it sometimes becomes a new token placed after merged vocab, creating a hole if previous process assumed contiguous ids. runtime's KV cache code assumes contiguous token id space for reserved block -> off-by-one.
kevin: solution options: 1) remap converted vocab to force reserved/placeholder tokens into a contiguous block at the start, 2) update runtime to not rely on absolute id ranges (bigger lift). I'd vote 1 for unblock.
anya: agree, easier. also noticed `config.json` had `special_tokens` listed in a different order than chat template expects (we expect `<|sys|>` at id 1). mismatch caused the chattemplate injection to use wrong ids.
ben_reid: can you run:```bash
python tools/hf_to_redwood.py 
  --input /tmp/mymodel 
  --output /tmp/mymodel-redwood 
  --preserve-sentinel 
  --force-contiguous-specials
```
anya: running now...
deploy-bot: deploy-check: tokenizer consistency test started for mymodel-redwood (job 8921)
anya: update — conversion + `--force-contiguous-specials` fixed the missing id hole. tokenizer check now shows contiguous block 0..15 reserved, token ids for text content start at 16. kv-cache error disappeared on a small smoke run.
lisa_ml: nice. open a PR to the conversion tool to make `--force-contiguous-specials` default for spm sources, and add a warning when `tokenizer.json` has gaps.
kevin: also update `chat_template` validation: assert that tokens referenced by templates exist and map to expected special ids. I added a tiny unit test in local.
anya: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/412 — adds remap, a `--dry-run` flag and a post-conversion check, plus test vectors.
ben_reid: will review. can we add a quick integration test that runs a tiny quantized eval and compares logits near tokens that used to be problematic?
lisa_ml: yes added to backlog, but for now we at least have the conversion guard. thanks everyone :rocket:
anya: summary for posterity: root cause = spm suffixpiece -> bpe token appended out-of-order creating id gap; effects = kv-cache index mismatch + chat template special token mismatch; fix = remap specials to contiguous block during conversion + config/chat-template validation.
kevin: tagging @infra-team FYI since runtime assumption surfaced here.
anya: closing thread once PR merges and CI green. :white_check_mark:
